_readme: Corrections to the mirrored OC model that cannot be derived from the export (#606).
Every entry here is a RECORDED OBSERVATION with its evidence written down, never an
inference the build could have made for itself. That is the whole point of the file:
the two upstream sources disagree in ways only a third check can settle, and once
settled the answer has to live somewhere durable. The probe sweep that produced the
ending->node mapping ran against tornprobability's live API and no longer runs, and
the tenant export carries only its RESULT (resolved/starved), not the per-ending
probabilities it decided from -- so a correction cannot be re-derived at build time.
Two kinds of entry, deliberately separate because they fix different things:
aliasEndings  { ourKey: ourOtherKey }
The API reports more endings than the flowchart draws terminals for, and the
surplus keys are additional labels for a terminal it already has. The alias
takes the target's node, so it prices from the same observations instead of
being starved at $0.
rewardFrom    { ourKey: crimesHubKey }
Crimes Hub numbers its endings by reward rank; tornprobability numbers them by
its own scheme. They usually agree, and where they do not, joining the published
reward by key name puts it on the wrong ending. A hub key named here is consumed
by the mapping and is NOT also joined to the ending of the same name.
disputedKind  { ourKey: 'good' | 'bad' }
The two services disagree about whether an ending is a success or a failure.
The value is what CRIMES HUB says; we do NOT adopt it. Recording the dispute
is the whole point -- it is surfaced on the page so a reader can see that a
figure is contested, rather than being silently resolved in either direction.

_evidence: Crimes Hub's own simulator, all six CPRs at 75 (2026-09-07), against tornprobability
at the same crew. Crimes Hub draws four good terminals; tornprobability reports eight
good endings. The surplus four are not separate outcomes -- their mass belongs to
terminals the diagram already has, and the grouping is exact:
Crimes Hub  Good End #3  = node _B8S1_  17.78%
tornprobability  goodEnding3 10.526 + goodEnding35 6.316 + goodEnding310 0.936 = 17.778
Crimes Hub  Good End #4  = node _B8S2_   5.93%
tornprobability  goodEnding4  3.509 + goodEnding45 2.104 + goodEnding410 0.312 =  5.925
Good End #1 (42.10 vs 42.105) and #2 (14.03 vs 14.035) match one-to-one, as do all
three bad ends, so the two services agree everywhere except this grouping.
Left starved, those four sat at $0 while holding 9.67% of the crime's probability,
and because a starved ending is priced-by-definition (#473) the panel reported the
result as COMPLETE: a firm $111,028,512 where the answer is $122,489,526.
TWO SEPARATE FINDINGS on this crime. The reward join below is settled; the
success/failure classification is NOT, and is recorded rather than resolved.
1. REWARD JOIN. Crimes Hub publishes four good endings; the diagram draws four
good terminals; tornprobability reports six good endings. Both the published
respect and the simulated probability identify the join, and they agree:
node      obs respect   hub respect   our prob   hub prob   our key
So Crimes Hub's goodEnding4 is our goodEnding6. Joined by key name it landed
on our goodEnding4 -- which is starved, has no node, and is therefore the one
ending on the crime with no observation to check it against.
2. DISPUTED CLASSIFICATION. Every terminal above matches ONE-TO-ONE, to within
0.005 points, so there is no deficit for our goodEnding4 and goodEnding5 to
fold into -- they are not surplus labels the way Blast from the Past's are.
They are extra SUCCESS mass that Crimes Hub does not have at all:
our success 91.588  -  hub success 84.91  =  6.678
goodEnding5 5.407   +  goodEnding4 1.267  =  6.674
our failure  8.412  +  6.674             = 15.086   vs hub failure 15.09
It closes to 0.004 points, and Crimes Hub's flowchart draws exactly two bad
ends we do not have -- the two it labels 'Bad End #5?' and 'Bad End #6?',
the only endings on the crime it marks with a question mark.
tornprobability counts these two outcomes as successes; Crimes Hub counts
them as failures. Both models are internally consistent and sum to 100%.
NOT RESOLVED, deliberately. The money is unaffected either way -- a failure
pays $0 and a starved ending is priced $0 -- so nothing is gained by picking
a side there. What IS affected is the headline success chance and the scope
verdict it drives: at Intermediate (costs 3, pays 4) this crew nets 0.66
scope per run at 91.59% and 0.40 at 84.91%. Overriding tornprobability's own
figure on the strength of a source that has marked both endings '?' would
trade one confident number for another. The disagreement is shown instead.
Observed 2026-09-07, all five CPRs at 75, both simulators.
